card.name: Punctuation ending a clause in old prose
card.fires_on: Semicolons, colons, dashes and commas that close a full clause in older, formal essay-style prose, just before an explanation or list follows. Mostly in 19th-century general or scientific writing.

modes.label: Semicolon or colon after a clause
modes.description: A semicolon or colon ends a complete statement and introduces a continuation or elaboration.
